feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows breadth across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes, and less repetition across sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure and progression within one organization, plus concrete platform details like Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, and AI-enabled search.  
- Good impact signals: website scale, audience size, internal publisher count, and ownership of modernization, governance, and studio build-out all add weight.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve scannability and make the CV feel sharper.  
- Add more outcome-based metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results would increase impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, campaign performance).  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation style varies between sections; “French (A2/Learning)” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and foreground scale/leadership: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading public-sector digital platforms, governance, and content operations.”
- Add one concrete signal of scope or impact from recent roles, e.g., “enterprise web modernization for 10,000+ page sites” or “high-volume communications reaching public-sector audiences at scale.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel structure tied to outcomes: “Drives web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search to improve discovery, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement.”
- Consider aligning “AI-enabled user experiences” with the rest of the CV by using “AI-enabled search and content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- “Analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “multimedia production” repeat core competencies almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas will make it feel more distinct and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize strategic capabilities over channel execution; move “multimedia production and livestream operations” later or shorten it.
- Consider a sharper version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Workflow automation and platform integration • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style by replacing “&” with “and” if used elsewhere in section headings/body copy.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already prominent in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills: “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize what was unique or high-value in each project: e.g., “AI-assisted legislative discovery,” “Drupal 10 campaign microsite,” “conference installation integrated with web experience.”
- Use consistent verb tense and structure; consider “Led/Developed/Built” across all items.
- If possible, add one concrete result, audience, or scale metric to 1–2 projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search,” microsite work, and advocacy video series overlap with the consultant and NACo experience bullets; keep the footer more portfolio-style rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider leading with it to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around 4–5 outcomes-focused bullets and avoid repeating NACo accomplishments already covered in prior roles and Recent Projects.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, and web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed/implemented/refined” instead of “consult/build/advise.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper lines, e.g.:
- Designed digital workflows, governance, and analytics systems to improve cross-channel communications operations.
- Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Led AI-enabled search strategy, defining retrieval approach, structured content workflows, and discovery UX.
- Provided CMS/front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: launch dates, traffic, adoption, publishing efficiency, search success, or reduced turnaround time.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite work overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level if those projects stay detailed below.
- Governance/analytics/web improvement also repeats the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize consultant scope and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget management for a national membership organization.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: include team size, budget, reporting improvements, production volume, cost savings from the in-house studio, or engagement gains from newsletters/social/video.
- Condense generic phrasing: replace “strengthened digital operations” with specifics such as governance model, publishing standards adopted, or planning system implemented.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization and infrastructure.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo roles and Recent Projects; emphasize building the studio and scaling capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as a softer precursor to the stronger Director-level accomplishments. Tighten it to emphasize what was distinctly owned at this level: operating cadence, newsletters, video series, and cross-team editorial coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day multi-channel digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video platforms, supporting advocacy and member engagement.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen ownership: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is too similar to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Expanded weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this role as formalizing/scaling the series, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, higher-signal language tied to recent work:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization  
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)  
- Public-sector advocacy communications  
- Audience-centered content strategy & information architecture
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” or “strategy” to sound more senior and operational.
- If space allows, align wording with measurable scope from recent roles elsewhere in the CV (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), but don’t force metrics into this section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than examples already shown in work experience and projects.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent work, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a curated value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section, so this version should emphasize higher-value capabilities and current strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS administration • CMS modernization and content architecture • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Put Drupal, CMS modernization, and AI-enabled search first since they align most directly with the 2022–present roles.
- Replace weaker/older platform mentions if not central to target roles; consider dropping SharePoint or Power Pages from this topline section and keeping them in “Technical + IT.”
- Use parallel phrasing and avoid mixing nouns with full phrases inconsistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic, and reserve full platform inventory for the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also echo core competencies; avoid repeating both unless they are differentiators for the target role.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for the most recent leadership roles, but the line reads as a generic keyword list. It would be stronger if grouped around business value and trimmed to avoid overlap with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Digital analytics and optimization” rather than a software inventory.
- Group items by function: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI” + “KPI framework development, executive reporting, SEO and performance analysis.”
- Consider this tighter rewrite: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- If you can support it elsewhere, add impact signals tied to recent roles: reporting for a 10,000+ page site, 3.5M annual page views, or organization-wide decision support.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Leadership reporting” is vague; “executive dashboarding” is sharper.
- Avoid repeating “analytics” language already covered in Core Competencies unless this section adds specific tools or methods.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with the “Multimedia & live event production” competency plus several NACo experience bullets. Make it more specific to current senior-level capability and tools/process ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Video, Studio & Live Event Production”
- Tighten and sharpen the list: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- If accurate, add one higher-value capability instead of a generic term like “editing,” e.g. “Run-of-show design” or “Technical direction”
- Keep this as a capability snapshot, not a duty list; use noun phrases and parallel structure throughout

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Livestreaming”; combine or differentiate
- This item partially duplicates “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies, so this version should be more tool-/execution-specific

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but as written it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and the core competency “Web & CMS administration.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant, recent platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise, 10,000+ page migration) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of just names: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; static publishing: GitHub Pages.”
- Use consistent grouping language to make it feel more intentional and less like a raw keyword dump.
- If Drupal is your clear flagship platform, lead with it and attach the strongest proof point from recent NACo work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills almost exactly.
- Consider deleting GitHub Pages here if it’s not supported elsewhere or materially important to target roles.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and slightly more senior by emphasizing practical application rather than basic languages.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API and tag implementation • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Drop version labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses that style; they feel dated for a senior candidate.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “JavaScript/jQuery” or removing it if it’s not central to recent work; keep the emphasis on current tools.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier such as “front-end implementation,” “light scripting,” or “deployment automation” to better match recent Drupal/CMS work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”). Differentiate this section by listing tools only, while keeping broader capabilities in Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may also overlap with workflow automation themes elsewhere; frame it as CI/deployment rather than general automation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow/systems” language already used in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Make it more selective and framed around automation/operations rather than general collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems**
- Tighten to the most relevant tools: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- If space allows, add light functional grouping: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow management:** Jira, Asana
- Consider replacing broad chat tools with higher-signal systems only if used operationally at depth; otherwise keep this section focused on workflow architecture.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **Slack • Teams** are general collaboration tools and add less value here than the workflow/automation platforms.
- **Basecamp • Trello** may feel redundant with **Jira • Asana** unless there is a specific reason to show all four.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and undersells your email/engagement leadership. Since recent roles emphasize large-scale email operations, this item should signal platform depth and campaign/CRM relevance more clearly.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing, CRM & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add 1–2 capability cues instead of only names, e.g.: email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Email” already appears repeatedly in Work Experience and the summary; avoid adding generic phrases like “email campaigns” unless tied to platform capability
- Higher Logic may be less recognizable alone; use the full product name if correct to avoid ambiguity

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show depth in analytics leadership. Since recent roles already prove these platforms, this item should be tighter and more capability-focused.

Suggested edit
- Replace the generic list with grouped phrasing: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • SEO/performance analysis • A/B testing • Executive dashboarding & KPI reporting”
- Swap “Dashboarding” for “Executive dashboarding & KPI reporting” to sound more senior and outcome-oriented.
- If space allows, add one stronger optimization term such as “conversion analysis” or “user behavior analysis” instead of the broad “SEO.”
- Keep only the most relevant tools named here; let work experience carry proof of implementation and scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider consolidating or differentiating one as tools and the other as capabilities.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already explicitly referenced in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale or output metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team-building impact: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer execution/results: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand member-facing communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add numbers: volume of livestreams/videos, audience growth, email/social reach, or website traffic improvements tied to the refresh.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or piloting the format here.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations language; keep this entry more tactical and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Make the second sentence more outcome-oriented: “Produced digital and multimedia content for program outreach, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this item to 1–2 lines since later roles better demonstrate broader digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media roles; avoid broad multimedia claims here.
- Don’t repeat video/editorial workflow language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only, with concise capability labels rather than repeating production functions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as tool-focused: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
- If you want light context, use tighter phrasing: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
- Move non-tool items out or relabel them as capabilities: replace with **Video editing • Audio editing** only if you need keyword coverage
- If possible, add proficiency or scale elsewhere in experience bullets, not here, e.g., studio built, recurring video series launched, podcast created
